records.name: Olivet Covenant Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on North 22nd Street with Sunday worship, a Wednesday Bible study and a page for people who are new to the church.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship and stay for the potluck after it, or join the Wednesday Bible study. The church started Connection Groups in 2026 so members and newcomers can build friendships.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, with a potluck right after. Wednesday Bible study at 1 pm in the basement lounge, with a Zoom option. The site asks people to confirm each week's meeting by email before they come.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, or fill out the newcomer form on the I'm New Here page and a leader will reach out to you.
first_step.basis: The I'm New Here page invites newcomers to send in a form and says a leader will reach out, and the 2026 Connection Groups are described as a way for newcomers to meet people.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 11 am and a potluck follows right after. The site does not say how long the service runs or what it is like, so the office can answer questions before you come. The site does not say visitors must pay, though it has an online giving link.
first_visit_tips: Call or email the church office before your first visit with any questions.
The church has a parking lot.
Stay after worship for the potluck if you want to meet people.

records.notes: Worship time comes from the Participate page, because the I'm New Here page and the bulletin archive list no service times. The Bible study confirmation email on the site is a seminary address, which I left out. The bulletin archive runs to October 4, 2026.

records.name: One River Alliance
records.summary: A group that brings neighbors, businesses, and community groups together along the Delaware riverfront. It runs the July 4th FreedomFest fireworks festival.
records.what_you_do: Come out for the free July 4th FreedomFest at Pleasant Hill Park. The alliance also starts new events during the year and invites ideas for next year's festival. The site does not describe volunteering or membership.

schedule.text: Each July 4th, a free fireworks festival at Pleasant Hill Park on the Delaware River, with a flag raising at 5 pm and fireworks at 9 pm.

locations.label: Pleasant Hill Park (Linden Ave. at the Delaware River)

cost.text: Free to attend. No tickets or registration needed.

first_step.how: Come to the free July 4th FreedomFest at Pleasant Hill Park. The next one is set for July 4, 2027, and details will be posted on the website as they come out.
first_step.basis: The festival is free and open to the public, with no tickets or registration needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival starts with a flag raising and the national anthem at 5 pm, then has live music, food trucks, vendors and family activities, with fireworks at 9 pm. It runs until about 9:30 pm. Admission is free and no tickets are needed.
first_visit_tips: Parking is not on the park grounds. Visitors park on State Road and nearby streets, and the group suggests a ride share.
Plan for the weather, since the festival goes ahead rain or shine.
Bring water and check the website before the day for any changes.

records.notes: The FreedomFest page title in the browser says 2025 while its body says 2026, so the 2026 date rests on the body text and on the homepage thanks to the 2026 sponsors. The site lists the director's address on a non-group domain, so I did not copy it. The newsletter form on the homepage is not working yet, so I did not recommend it. The group has no membership or volunteer page.

records.name: Ordinarie Heroes
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps young people build leadership, school and career skills. It also runs a mobile pantry, an educational farm and nutrition workshops.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in weekly in-person leadership sessions, tutoring, film and photo workshops, and college and career prep. The Inspire program is for young people aged 11 and up. Adults and young people can help with the food pantry, tutoring or office work, and adults can sign up as mentors.

schedule.text: Program office open Monday to Friday, 2 to 8 pm, and on Saturdays for scheduled events. Leadership sessions run weekly in person. Food pantry volunteer shifts run on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, 9 am to 2 pm, February through December.

cost.text: No cost listed on the site

first_step.how: Fill out the online volunteer form on the Connect page for a food pantry shift (2nd and 4th Saturdays, 9 am to 2 pm), or call (215) 385-5135 to ask about the next leadership session.
first_step.basis: The site has online forms for volunteers, mentors and young people, plus a phone and email for questions. It does not describe what a first session or shift is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: A food pantry shift runs 9 am to 2 pm on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays. Volunteers check stock, organize new items, bag groceries and interact with families in Hunting Park. The site does not describe a training or what a leadership session looks like.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 385-5135 or email info@ohmovement.org before your first shift to confirm the time.
The office at 2066 W Hunting Park Ave is open Monday to Friday, 2 to 8 pm.
Donations of supplies are accepted all year, and the site keeps a list of current needs.

records.notes: The site lists no dated events or news. The events page has an upcoming heading with nothing under it, so status stays probably active. The mailing address (828 S Alden Street) is not a place to visit, so I left it out. The site does not say whether volunteers need a background check, training or a minimum age. The Inspire program age floor is 11, and other program ages are not stated.

records.name: Our Lady of Calvary Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Knights Road in the Far Northeast with Sunday Masses, a weekday morning Mass, a Saturday vigil and Saturday confession.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or join a parish ministry such as the Adoration Chapel, the ushers, the choirs, the Knights of Columbus or the Legion of Mary. The parish also runs a school, and the ministries page lists a contact person for each group.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Sunday Masses at 6:30, 8 and 10 am and at noon, plus a 6 pm Mass in February, April, June, October and December. Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 6:30 am (September to June) and at 8 am. Saturday confession 3:45 to 4:45 pm, or by appointment at the rectory.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass or the Saturday 5 pm vigil, or call the parish office at 215-637-7515 with questions.
first_step.basis: Masses are open to anyone and the office phone is listed, but the site describes no welcome process for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. The website does not describe the service, how long it runs, or what visitors do during it. The office at 215-637-7515 is the best place for those questions.
first_visit_tips: Call the parish office at 215-637-7515 for parking, transit and directions, since the site does not list them.
The Saturday vigil at 5 pm is an option if Sunday mornings are hard to make.

records.notes: The parish's own pages list four Sunday Masses (6:30, 8, 10 am and noon) and a Saturday vigil at 5 pm. The archdiocese listing also has a 6 pm Sunday Mass in some months, which the parish pages do not mention, so the office should confirm it. The directions page describes only parish boundaries. The ministries page lists contacts but no meeting times. The latest bulletin in the archive is dated August 2, 2026.

records.name: Our Lady of Consolation Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Tulip Street with Masses in English and Spanish, a Latin Mass at 1:30 pm, and a Saturday evening vigil.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in English, Spanish or Latin, or join a parish ministry such as the Food Cupboard, the Giving Tree Committee or the youth ministries. Children and teens can take part in P.R.E.P. religious education, and adults exploring the Catholic faith can join R.C.I.A. The parish also holds a Wednesday Rosary at 6:30 pm in the church, open to everyone.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 and 10:15 am, at 11:30 am in Spanish, and at 1:30 pm in the Latin form. Saturday vigil at 5 pm. Weekday Mass at 8 am, and at 7 pm in Spanish on Wednesday; 9 am on federal holidays. Saturday confession 4 to 4:45 pm. Wednesday Rosary at 6:30 pm in the church.

first_step.how: Come to any listed Mass, or call the parish office Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, to ask about visiting or to register as a new parishioner.
first_step.basis: The site has a general welcome message and explains how a new parishioner registers: download the form from the website, then send it to the office or call.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, with services in English, Spanish and Latin. The site does not say how long a Mass lasts or what happens during it. The office is open Monday to Thursday and closed on Fridays, so call on those days if you have questions.
first_visit_tips: The office is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, and closed Fridays, so plan your call for those hours.
The parish secretary speaks English and Spanish.
Download the New Parishioner Registration form from the website if you want to join the parish.

records.notes: The Spanish Mass schedule page shows its times only as an image, which I could not read, so the Mass times come from the parish info page and match the tier 1 listing. Tier 1 said the archdiocese lists no community programs, but the parish's own site lists ministries (a food cupboard, a Giving Tree Committee and youth ministries), so what_you_do was updated. The religious education page lists two different email addresses for the director, so I did not record one. The parish site lists no parking or transit details.

records.name: Our Lady of Hope Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 5200 North Broad Street with Sunday Masses, a Spanish Mass at 11 am and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. The parish names an African American Apostolate and a Hispanic Apostolate, each with a contact person, and a St. Vincent de Paul conference (call 267-297-5548). The site gives no meeting times for the apostolates.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 am in English and 11 am in Spanish. Saturday Mass at 4 pm in English. Weekday Mass Tuesday to Friday at 8 am in the chapel, in English. The parish has no Monday Mass. Saturday confession 3:30 to 4 pm, or by appointment through the office.

first_step.how: Come to the 9 am English or 11 am Spanish Sunday Mass, or call the parish office at 215-329-8100 to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: The About Us section calls the parish welcoming and invites newcomers to contact the parish about joining.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Spanish is offered at the 11 am Sunday Mass only. The site does not describe what a Mass is like or how new parishioners join, so call the office with questions.
first_visit_tips: Pick the 11 am Sunday Mass if you want the Spanish service.
The parish office number is 215-329-8100. The site has no parking or transit notes, so call before you come.
Confession is on Saturday from 3:30 to 4 pm, or by appointment through the office.

records.notes: Tier 1 listed Sunday Masses at 8:30, 10:30 (Spanish) and 12:30, and weekday Mass Monday to Saturday at 8:30, from the archdiocese listing. The parish's own homepage, checked twice, lists 9 am English and 11 am Spanish on Sunday, 4 pm on Saturday, 8 am Tuesday to Friday in the chapel, and no Monday Mass, so the record follows the parish. The office should confirm, because the archdiocese listing may be out of date. The site describes the address as the Church of the Holy Child. The contact page is only a Google Form. The most recent visible bulletin is dated October 4, 2026.

records.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 63rd Street and Lancaster Avenue with Sunday Masses, including a Latin High Mass, and weekday Mass with Lauds.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass or to Thursday Adoration, which includes Vespers and Benediction at 7 pm. Families are welcome. The parish also lists a Lourdes for Life program and pilgrimages, though the site gives few details. The site links a 2026 to 2027 registration form for First Penance and First Communion.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am, 9:30 am (Latin High Mass), 11:30 am and 8 pm. Weekday Masses at 6:30 am and 8:30 am, with Lauds at 8 am; times shift a little in summer. Saturday morning Mass and a 4 pm vigil. Thursday Adoration after Mass, with a 4 pm Rosary and 7 pm Vespers and Benediction. Confession most days, including Saturday 2:30 to 3:45 pm.

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. Visitors are not expected to give.

access.notes: For the October 2026 pilgrimage day, the site named a ramped entrance on the Lancaster Avenue side and an accessible restroom trailer. It does not say whether that entrance is used at ordinary Masses.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass or to Thursday Adoration. To join the parish, use the registration page on the website or call 215-473-1669.
first_step.basis: The I'm New Here page is written for newcomers, says families are welcome, and points to the parish registration page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass and Adoration are free, and visitors are not expected to put money in the offering. Families are welcome, and the parish says a restless child is fine; a parent may step out to the vestibule and come back when the child settles. The site does not give how long Mass or Adoration lasts, so ask the office if you have questions.
first_visit_tips: There is no parking lot. Park on the street in the Overbrook Farms area and walk to the church.
On Sundays and holy days, arrive early, since students from nearby St. Joseph's University sometimes take up street spaces during the school year.
Call 215-473-1669 about transit or access, since the site does not give those details.

records.notes: Tier 1 gave the church as 63rd St. and Lancaster Ave. The I'm New Here page gives the church as 6301 Woodbine Ave. and the mailing address as 6315 Lancaster Ave., so the record uses the church address. Tier 1's Saturday confession (2:30 to 4 pm) and Thursday Adoration (7 am to 7:20 pm) differ from the parish's listing (confession Saturday 2:30 to 3:45 pm; Adoration after Mass with Vespers at 7 pm), so the parish's times are used. The contact page's office hours are placeholder text, so none are recorded. The Saturday morning Mass has no time on the site, so none is given here.

notes: All seven sites had their own visitor, volunteer or bulletin pages, so the single WebSearch was not needed; searches_used is 0. No pages were blocked and no rate limiting was seen. Four groups had tier 1 details that conflicted with the group's own site (Our Lady of Hope Mass times, Our Lady of Lourdes address and confession and adoration times, Our Lady of Consolation ministries, Our Lady of Calvary Sunday Mass list). The records follow the parish sites; office confirmation is advised for the Hope and Calvary Mass lists. Olivet's 2025 banner names two partner groups (Red Letter Christians and Freedom Road), but the page gives no link to them, so they are not in leads_only. Personal or seminary email addresses published on two group sites were left out. Per-group fetches: 3 to 5, under the six-per-group limit.
